players.product: 1.6T PAM4 DSP, TIAs, drivers, silicon photonics light engines, coherent DSP, custom XPU silicon

quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 demo: Marvell is showing what it calls the first 2nm 400G/lane optical PAM4 demonstration. The release positions it as low-power, ultra-high-speed optical connectivity for scaling AI infrastructure, enabling the transition to 3.2T data center connectivity. 400G/lane PAM4 itself was demonstrated before (earlier call entries on this node); the new element here is the 2nm process node. A demonstration only - the release makes no shipping or production claim.
quarterly_data.figure: first 2nm 400G/lane optical PAM4 demonstration; enabling the transition to 3.2T data center connectivity

quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 demo: what Marvell calls the first live demonstration of 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ with MACsec - an 800G ZR/ZR+ OSFP pluggable powered by the Marvell Libra 2nm coherent DSP that integrates media access control security (MACsec). New versus the node: the 2nm 800G DSP is named (Libra) and shown in an OSFP ZR/ZR+ pluggable with integrated MACsec, extending Marvell's coherent DSP and COLORZ pluggable portfolios for hyperscale AI and cloud data center networks. The release gives no sampling, shipping or customer detail.
quarterly_data.figure: first live demonstration of 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ OSFP pluggable with MACsec, on the Libra 2nm coherent DSP

quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 demos: what Marvell calls the first 2nm 1.6T ZR and 1.6T coherent-lite O-band demonstrations, powered by next-generation Marvell DSPs announced earlier this year and optimized for high-bandwidth connectivity within and between data center facilities; the release says they pave the way for 3.2T connectivity. The 2nm 1.6T ZR/ZR+ DSP announcement is already on the node from earlier calls; the new elements are the 2nm 1.6T coherent-lite O-band and both being shown as demonstrations. No production claim in the release.
quarterly_data.figure: first 2nm 1.6T ZR and 1.6T coherent-lite O-band demonstrations; paving the way for 3.2T connectivity

quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 demo of the Marvell 102.4T co-packaged optics (CPO) platform, which integrates optics directly with AI accelerators and switch silicon. The release says the platform is demonstrated at 102.4 Tbps with 200G-per-lane silicon photonics, and gives the rationale as per-lane speeds and multi-rack AI pods pushing past copper's reach limits. Shown as a demonstration; the release gives no sampling, customer or production timing.
quarterly_data.figure: 102.4T CPO platform demonstrated at 102.4 Tbps with 200G-per-lane silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: Optical DSP lineage as stated in the release, which Marvell lists as industry firsts: the first 5nm 200G/lane 1.6T Marvell Nova DSPs in 2023, the 3nm 1.6T Ara platform in 2024 and the 2nm 800G Libra DSPs announced earlier this year. Marvell says its 2nm connectivity portfolio now includes optical PAM4, coherent-lite PAM4/IMDD and ZR/ZR+ coherent solutions in the 2nm node, aimed at interconnects between XPUs, CPUs, accelerators and memory resources.
quarterly_data.figure: 5nm 200G/lane 1.6T Nova DSPs (2023); 3nm 1.6T Ara platform (2024); 2nm 800G Libra DSPs (announced earlier this year)

quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 showcase scope: Marvell says it is showing 38 advanced technology demos, including the 102.4T CPO platform and additional demos developed with its partner ecosystem (partners not named). Beyond the 2nm demonstrations, its ECOC booth covers 224G SerDes, 1.6T optics, coherent interconnects and optical memory fabrics.
quarterly_data.figure: 38 advanced technology demos; 224G SerDes, 1.6T optics, coherent interconnects, optical memory fabrics

quarterly_data.signal: Xi Wang, senior vice president and general manager, Connectivity Business Unit, said AI data center operators need optical interconnect technologies that deliver higher bandwidth, lower power and greater security across every part of the network, and described the ECOC demonstrations as meant to help hyperscaler and cloud data center customers. The release frames the same need as AI data center architectures scale from 1.6T to 3.2T and beyond across AI scale-up, scale-out and scale-across domains. Xi Wang also holds an ECOC fireside chat on new and emerging optical technologies.
